scopeReview: PSO-1.A/PSO-1.A.1: absolute and relative location, space/place, flows, distance decay, time-space compression and pattern. Aggregation item applies spatial-pattern reasoning without changing official topic IDs. All fictional data are original.
varietyReview: Eleven distinct applications, four interpreted stimuli; foundation/intermediate/challenging items, four key positions and all five geographic skills. No real-country statistics or copyrighted question sources.
repetitionReview: Reviewed against Topics1.1–1.3: this set focuses on spatial concepts rather than repeating map-type identification, data-collection methods or clinic decisions. Bridge, communication, place identity, remittance flows, density/arrangement and aggregation ask different relationships.

questions.correctOption: The businesses form a linear pattern; its cause is not shown.
questions.independentReview: Inspected all five coordinates: every y equals 15; sorted x values are20,35,50,65,80. The points span a line rather than a two-dimensional grid or cluster. No causal feature is supplied.

questions.correctOption: Town Q is more accessible despite its greater straight-line distance.
questions.independentReview: Independently compared20<45 km but50>25 minutes. The criterion is explicitly time, so only Q wins; no route speed or actual transport mode is assumed.

questions.correctOption: The share visiting decreases as distance increases, without establishing that distance is the only cause.
questions.independentReview: Checked the ordered distances5,15,25 and shares60,30,10. Successive differences in shares are negative; equal denominators prevent size confounding but do not establish exclusive causality.

questions.correctOption: Higher transit-stop counts occur with higher shop counts, but causal direction is undetermined.
questions.independentReview: Independently sorted districts by stops0,5,10 and verified shops4,20,40 also increase. The first increment is16 shops and second20, refuting a fixed four-shops-per-stop rule as well as causal certainty.

questions.correctOption: Their relative accessibility improves while their absolute locations remain fixed.
questions.independentReview: Held coordinates constant and varied only network travel time. This uniquely supports a change in relative accessibility, not absolute location, identity or physical separation.

questions.correctOption: Faster communication reduces the effective separation of distant collaborators.
questions.independentReview: Separated communication latency from physical distance, time zones and universal access. The actual stated change is the time required to connect the two endpoints.

questions.correctOption: A sense of place shaped by shared meanings and experiences
questions.independentReview: Checked the evidence: shared cultural use and resident meaning, not changed dimensions, coordinates or travel data. The correct inference is bounded to described residents, avoiding a universal identity claim.

questions.correctOption: A flow linking places through the movement of funds
questions.independentReview: Verified the encoded object is money, not migrating people. A directional relation between origin and destination is sufficient for a flow without implying uniform regional conditions.

questions.correctOption: The districts have equal overall school density but different arrangements.
questions.independentReview: Independently formed both densities as12/A for identical A, while retaining distinct within-area configurations. No claim of equal local access follows from the aggregate equality.

questions.correctOption: It shows that cultural and network connections can modify a general distance-related tendency.
questions.independentReview: Tested the universal alternatives against the limited single-pair evidence. Cultural affinity is explicitly supplied, so the warranted conclusion is a conditional limitation, not a denial of all distance effects.

questions.correctOption: Whether adjacent neighborhoods exchange more visits than nonadjacent neighborhoods
questions.independentReview: Identified exactly which variables survive aggregation: province totals remain, neighborhood identities and pair links do not. Only the adjacency question requires information explicitly discarded.
